docRequirement: whats-new/index.md:92 binds us to two session-scoped plugin side-load flags: "**Plugins load from `.zip` archives and URLs**: `--plugin-dir` now accepts `.zip` files, and `--plugin-url` fetches a plugin archive for the current session." The reference pages fix the semantics: plugins/cli-reference.md#flags-that-load-a-plugin-for-one-session (was line 763 of the retired plugins-reference page) — plugins may be provided "Through `claude --plugin-dir` or `claude --plugin-url`, for the duration of a session"; plugins.md:322 — "The flag also accepts a `.zip` archive of the plugin directory"; plugins.md:328 — a `--plugin-dir` plugin with the same name as an installed one "takes precedence for that session", except where managed settings force-enable/force-disable it; plugins.md:344 — for `--plugin-url` Claude Code "fetches the archive at startup and loads it for that session only", and on fetch/validity failure "it starts without the plugin and records a plugin load error"; both flags are repeatable (plugins.md:340, :349) and `--plugin-url` also accepts space-separated URLs in one quoted argument (plugins.md:355). plugins/cli-reference.md#flags-that-load-a-plugin-for-one-session (was line 1096 of the retired plugins-reference page) — session-loaded plugins "have no installed record", so a bare `plugin list` must not show them.
current: No reader for either flag exists in first-party source. `apps/cli/src/index.ts:78-165` is the whole `parseArgs` switch and its `default:` arm (`:160-166`) pushes any unknown `-`-prefixed argument into `rest`, which never reaches a plugin loader; the accepted flag list contains neither name. `grep -rna -F 'plugin-dir'` and `'plugin-url'` over `packages/*/src apps/*/src` return 0 hits (run with `-a`, so NUL-byte files are not skipped); the only `plugin-dir` occurrences in the tree are vendored — `packages/pi-agent-server/dist/index.js:344897` is the bundled Claude Agent SDK's own argv builder for its `plugins: [{type:'local', path}]` option, a capability we ship and never call. `apps/cli/src/index.ts:2060-2066` exposes only `plugin validate <path>` / `plugin list` / `plugin details <name>`, all read-only. The Claude backend shuts the SDK's own route off deliberately: `packages/shared/src/agent/claude-agent.ts:1629` hardcodes `plugins: []` with the comment at `:1627` "No plugins — skills are handled by BaseAgent.chat() via read-before-execute". There is no ephemeral plugin concept at all: `packages/shared/src/plugins/types.ts:4` is `export type PluginScope = 'user/global' | 'workspace' | 'project'` and every install is persistent; `grep -rnai 'sideload|side-load|ephemeral plugin|sessionPlugins'` over `*/src` returns 0. A session's capability set is assembled exclusively from the committed registry: `packages/server-core/src/bootstrap/storage-runtime.ts:644` reads `deps.pluginStore.readInstalledRegistry()`, derives `activeEntries` at `:648-651`, and feeds only those to `resolvePluginProjectionCandidates(activeEntries, selectedScope)` at `:729` — there is no second input. Acquisition from a URL or a local path does exist, but only as a persistent install: `packages/shared/src/plugins/source-resolver.ts:85` classifies `kind: 'url'` and `:97` `kind: 'local-path'`, dispatched at `packages/shared/src/plugins/install-service.ts:514` and `:520`. And that path cannot open a plugin `.zip`. Zip extraction is MCPB-only on both routes: `install-service.ts:569-570` gates the local-file branch on `isZipArchive(...) && (hasMcpbArchiveExtension(sourcePath) || await hasRootMcpbManifest(sourcePath))`, and `:805-806` gates the archive-URL branch the same way; `hasRootMcpbManifest` demands a ROOT `manifest.json` with an MCPB `manifest_version`/`dxt_version` of 0.1–0.3 and a `server` object (`packages/shared/src/plugins/mcpb-archive.ts:33-35`, `:152-165`), and `extractMcpbArchive` throws "MCPB archive must contain a valid root manifest.json." at `:39`. A Claude-layout zip (rooted at `.claude-plugin/plugin.json`) misses that gate, so locally it falls through to `copyInside(...)` at `install-service.ts:574` and is stored as an opaque FILE, and over a URL it falls to `extractArchiveFile(...)` at `:809`, which is a tar-only extractor (`extractTar({file, cwd, strip})`, `install-service.ts:1314-1352`) and cannot read a zip at all. Normalization then fails with `plugin.format.unsupported_format` (`install-service.ts:317`, `:2688-2689`; `format-adapters.ts:252`, `:403`) because `wrapStandaloneSkillFile` only rescues a lone `SKILL.md` (`install-service.ts:2617-2619`). Committed positive control for that absence: `packages/shared/src/plugins/__tests__/mcpb.test.ts:77-88` ("preserves the legacy local-file path for an ordinary ZIP") asserts `readdirSync(staged.rawDirectory)` equals `['ordinary.zip']` and that `plugin/plugin.json` was never unpacked, while `:90-100` proves the same rig unpacks a `.zip` that does carry a root `manifest.json`. The desktop's only local-archive surface reinforces the same MCPB-only shape: `apps/electron/src/preload/mcpb-import.ts:17` filters the native picker to `extensions: ['mcpb', 'dxt']` and `:36` rejects anything else via `hasMcpbArchiveExtension` before a byte is read, and the server twin `snapshotMcpbArchive` re-rejects at `packages/server-core/src/handlers/rpc/marketplace.ts:464` with `marketplace.mcpb.invalid_archive` (`:416`), issuing the proposal with `detectedFormat: 'mcpb'` hardcoded at `:258`.
divergence: Two separate absences, both real, neither a renamed key or a wrong value. (a) SESSION SCOPE — the whole mechanism is missing, not narrowed. Nothing in this fork can load a plugin for one session and forget it: `PluginScope` (`plugins/types.ts:4`) has three persistent members and the capability assembly (`storage-runtime.ts:729`) accepts only committed `PluginInstalledEntryV2[]`. The nearest shipped behaviour — install from a URL or local path — is the opposite of the documented one: it writes an installed record, so it violates plugins/cli-reference.md#flags-that-load-a-plugin-for-one-session (was line 1096 of the retired plugins-reference page) ("no installed record") and plugins.md:344 ("that session only"), and it offers no name-override-for-this-session semantics (plugins.md:328). (b) ARCHIVE FORMAT — present but for the wrong format. We have a hardened zip extractor (`mcpb-archive.ts:37-150`) and we refuse to point it at a plugin bundle: the gates at `install-service.ts:569-570`/`:805-806` require an MCPB root `manifest.json`, so a `.zip` of a plugin directory is either stored as an opaque file or handed to a tar extractor. That half is genuinely `built-partial` inside an otherwise `not-built` feature. Note also which flag is unimplementable-as-written and which is not: `--plugin-dir` is a Claude Code CLI flag and our product's primary surface is the Electron app, so the faithful equivalent is a session-scoped side-load input on the session-create boundary plus the CLI flags for `apps/cli`; the archive-format half has a direct, surface-independent fix.

change.what: Split the format-agnostic extractor out of `extractMcpbArchive` (:37-55) and `extractOpenZip` (:57-150) into an exported `extractZipArchive(archivePath, targetDirectory, options?: { strip?: number; allowExecutable?: (relativePath: string) => boolean })`. Only two things in there are MCPB-specific and both must move behind options: the root-manifest precondition at :38-39, and the executable-entry rule at :111-113 (`policy.serverType === 'binary' && relativePath === policy.binaryEntryPoint`) — for a plugin zip the predicate is 'any declared plugin executable', default deny. Keep every guard as-is: entry cap :82-84, per-entry and total byte caps :85-91, canonical duplicate-path check :93-98, symlink refusal :104-106, entry-type whitelist :108-110, `assertContained` :117, `flags: 'wx'` and mode clamp :117-124. `extractMcpbArchive` becomes a thin wrapper that reads the policy via `readArchivePolicy` and calls the generic extractor with the MCPB predicate — so no MCPB behaviour changes.

Local branch: at :569-575, when `isZipArchive(bytes.subarray(0,4))` is true but the MCPB gate fails, call the new `extractZipArchive(sourcePath, staged.rawDirectory, { strip: 1 })` instead of `copyInside(...)` at :574 — with `strip` applied only when the zip has exactly one top-level directory (plugins.md:322 calls it 'a `.zip` archive of the plugin directory', and real archives appear both ways). Archive-URL branch: at :805-810, sniff the downloaded bytes and route zip → `extractZipArchive`, everything else → the existing `extractArchiveFile` at :809; today a zip URL reaches the tar extractor and throws. Apply `MAX_PLUGIN_ARCHIVE_ENTRIES` / `MAX_PLUGIN_EXTRACTED_BYTES` (the limits `extractArchiveFile` enforces at :1329-1338) to the zip path so both routes share one budget. Also rename the fixed staging filename `artifact.tgz` at :800, which is now a lie for a zip.

New file. Takes `{ pluginDirs: string[]; pluginUrls: string[]; sessionId: string }`, stages each through the EXISTING `PluginInstallService.createInstallPlanFromSource` → `stageInstall` → `normalizeStagedInstall` (`install-service.ts:247`, `:292`) into a per-session temp root, and returns in-memory `PluginInstalledEntryV2[]` synthesized from the normalized manifest plus `computeNormalizedBundleHash` — WITHOUT calling `PluginStoreV2.install()` (`store-v2.ts:191`). Reuse `PluginOriginSource` values `'local-path'` / `'url'` (`plugins/types.ts:35-41`); do NOT add a new variant, because `PluginOrigin` is persisted with the installed record and a new value would be a registry-schema change for entries that are never written. Per-plugin failures must be collected as `PluginDiagnostic`s and must NOT abort session start (plugins.md:344: 'it starts without the plugin and records a plugin load error'). Delete the temp root on session teardown.

Do NOT extend `PluginScope` with a session/ephemeral member: it is the persisted activation scope read by the capability policy store, and adding a value crosses a persistence boundary for a plugin that is by definition never persisted. Add instead a small non-persisted `PluginSessionSideload { origin: 'plugin-dir' | 'plugin-url'; source: string }` used only in memory and on the session-create wire.

Add an optional `sessionSideloadEntries?: PluginInstalledEntryV2[]` to `CapabilityInputsV2Deps` and merge it into `activeEntries` right after :648-651, before `trustedProjectOverlay` (:652) and `byInstance`/`byKey` (:653-654), so `resolvePluginProjectionCandidates(activeEntries, selectedScope)` at :729 sees them. Precedence per plugins.md:328: a side-loaded plugin with the same `pluginKey` REPLACES the installed entry for this resolve — except that the managed filters already in the `:730-749` predicate must still decide (`isManagedPluginAllowed`, `resolveManagedPluginActivation` force-enable/force-disable), which they will because they key on `candidate.pluginKey`. Leave the safe-mode short-circuit at :629 exactly where it is: `--plugin-dir`/`--plugin-url` must load nothing under `NESSY_SAFE_MODE`, and returning `SAFE_MODE_INPUTS` before any read already achieves that.

Add repeatable `--plugin-dir <path>` and `--plugin-url <url>` cases to the switch (they must accumulate into arrays, not overwrite — plugins.md:340/:349), and split a single `--plugin-url` value on whitespace into multiple URLs (plugins.md:355). Thread both onto the session-create request. Add the two lines to the usage text next to `--safe-mode` (:2031) and cover the parse in `apps/cli/src/commands.test.ts` alongside the existing `--safe-mode` case at :37-38.

Carry the side-load list on the session-create boundary and validate it server-side with the same discipline as `--workspace-dir`: the server resolves and contains the path itself and never trusts a client-supplied absolute path, and a URL is fetched by the server, not the renderer. This is a wire-schema addition — a risk trigger in this repo, so it needs the expanded boundary check on the final diff.

This is the only local-archive picker in the desktop app and it rejects a plugin `.zip` at :36 before reading a byte. Widen `filters` to include `zip` (or add a sibling picker/spec) and stop making `hasMcpbArchiveExtension` the admission test — route non-MCPB zips to the plugin-zip path instead of returning `UNSUPPORTED_MCPB` (:20-24).

The server twin of the picker gate: :464 rejects any zip without a root MCPB manifest with `marketplace.mcpb.invalid_archive` (:416). Make it probe for a plugin layout too (`.claude-plugin/plugin.json`, or `plugin.json`, at the root or one level down) and return the detected format, so `proposalRegistry.issue({ ..., detectedFormat: 'mcpb' })` at :258 stops being hardcoded and `assertManagedMcpbSnapshotUnchanged` (:283) keeps guarding the right snapshot. The `.mcpb` snapshot filename at :461/:468 also needs to stop asserting a format it no longer knows.

change.symbol: 'preserves the legacy local-file path for an ordinary ZIP' (:77-88)
change.what: This test currently ASSERTS the divergence — `readdirSync(staged.rawDirectory) === ['ordinary.zip']` and no unpacked `plugin/plugin.json`. Invert it: an ordinary plugin-layout zip must unpack and normalize through the claude/nessy adapter. Keep :90-100 ('positively identifies a root MCPB manifest even when the suffix is .zip') unchanged as the MCPB-precedence control, and add a negative case for a zip that is neither MCPB nor a plugin layout (must still fail with `plugin.format.unsupported_format`).

blastRadius: Crosses a wire boundary and sits one field away from a persistence boundary — both risk triggers here. Readers of the changed surfaces: `resolvePluginProjectionCandidates` (`plugins/projection-candidates.ts:139`) and its 16 callers, including `packages/shared/src/capabilities/resolver.ts` and the tests `capabilities/__tests__/plugin-components-projection.test.ts`, `plugins/__tests__/unified-adapter-conformance.test.ts` (:85, :521, :527, :604) and `plugins/__tests__/core-adapter-lifecycle.test.ts:100`; `buildCapabilityResolutionInputsV2` (`server-core/src/bootstrap/storage-runtime.ts:622`) and the safe-mode gate suite `server-core/src/bootstrap/__tests__/safe-mode-capability-gate.test.ts`. The zip-extractor split is read by both artifact routes in `plugins/install-service.ts` (:514 local-path, :520 archive-url) and by the MCPB upload path in `server-core/src/handlers/rpc/marketplace.ts` (:254, :464) plus the Electron preload picker (`apps/electron/src/preload/mcpb-import.ts`), so a regression there breaks existing `.mcpb`/`.dxt` import, not only the new case — `plugins/__tests__/mcpb.test.ts` is the guard and one of its assertions must be inverted deliberately. PERSISTENCE: do not let a side-loaded entry reach `PluginStoreV2.install()` (`plugins/store-v2.ts:191`) or the activation policy store; if one leaked it would create a content-addressed cache directory under `PLUGINS_DIR` and an `active[pluginKey]` mapping that outlives the session, which is exactly what plugins/cli-reference.md#flags-that-load-a-plugin-for-one-session (was line 1096 of the retired plugins-reference page) forbids. `PluginOriginSource` (`plugins/types.ts:35`) and `PluginScope` (`:4`) are both persisted shapes — the plan above deliberately touches neither. WIRE: the session-create request gains a field, so `packages/shared/src/protocol/` validators, the Electron `channel-map.ts`/preload bridge and `apps/cli` all move together. Also downstream of a side-loaded plugin: per-executable-hash hook trust (`plugins/hooks-automation.ts`, `CapabilityTrustStore`) decides whether its hooks may run at all, the managed-policy filters at `storage-runtime.ts:730-749` must keep their veto, and `capabilityGeneration` must change when the side-load set changes or a resumed session will serve a stale capability snapshot. `plugin list` must keep excluding session plugins unless the flag precedes the subcommand (plugins/cli-reference.md#flags-that-load-a-plugin-for-one-session (was line 1096 of the retired plugins-reference page)), which affects `apps/cli/src/plugin.ts` and `apps/cli/src/plugin.test.ts:215`. The Claude backend's `plugins: []` (`shared/src/agent/claude-agent.ts:1629`) is a separate decision with its own recorded reason and is out of scope.
userImpact: Two concrete failures today. (1) A plugin author cannot try a plugin without installing it. There is no equivalent of `claude --plugin-dir ./my-plugin`: the only way in is Plugins → install, which commits an entry to the plugin registry and an activation record, so testing an iteration means install → test → uninstall, and a local copy can never temporarily shadow the same plugin already installed from a marketplace (plugins.md:328). (2) A plugin shipped as a `.zip` cannot be installed at all, by any route. In the desktop app the native picker (Create ▾ → import) is filtered to `.mcpb`/`.dxt` (`apps/electron/src/preload/mcpb-import.ts:17`), so `my-plugin.zip` is not even selectable; forcing it through returns the toast `plugins.mcpbUnsupported` with detail `marketplace.mcpb.invalid_archive`. Reaching the same file through the install-source resolver instead stages the zip as an opaque file and the install fails with `plugin.format.unsupported_format`. A zip hosted at a URL — the doc's stated use case, 'a CI build artifact' (plugins.md:344) — reaches the tar-only extractor and dies with `plugin.install.archive_fetch_failed`. Only an MCPB extension (root `manifest.json`, `manifest_version` 0.1–0.3) unpacks. The name collision makes this worse than a plain gap: a `.zip` that happens to be an MCPB bundle installs fine, so the failure looks arbitrary from the outside.
